# Kynoptic

> A local-first activity awareness layer for Windows. Kynoptic records
> which applications you use, when your machine is busy, and what
> changes on your system - entirely on your machine - and answers
> questions about it later through a CLI, a local dashboard, or MCP.

## What it is

- 40 system monitors (foreground window/app switches, keyboard/mouse
  activity counts, idle time, battery, network, devices, processes,
  audio, brightness, Wi-Fi, and more). 14 are enabled by default
  (native Win32 APIs on their main collection paths; the network
  monitor falls back to a bounded netstat.exe call, 3-second timeout,
  when its native path is unavailable); 26 more are opt-in.
- Raw events are stored untouched in SQLite. Aggregate tables are
  derived read caches only; the raw layer is append-only and is never
  truncated or cleaned up automatically.
- Status: v0.7.0, active development. Language: Rust. License:
  Apache-2.0.

## Privacy boundary

- No account, no telemetry, no analytics. Data never leaves the machine
  by default; the only unsolicited network call is the tray's
  once-a-day version check (GitHub), and the `update` subcommand only
  runs when the user explicitly invokes it (both hit GitHub releases).
- Keyboard and mouse are stored as per-minute counts only - never key
  contents. Per-key frequency counts (used by the dashboard heatmap) are
  on by default and can be disabled in settings.
- The dashboard HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 only. The MCP server is
  a stdio process (JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout) and has no network
  socket of any kind.
- Uninstalling keeps your data by default: the uninstaller's delete
  prompt defaults to No, and a silent uninstall keeps the data
  directory (`<install dir>\data`) without asking. Only an explicit
  Yes, confirmed after an irreversible-delete warning, deletes it; if
  kept, the uninstaller shows where the data was left.

## Architecture (four crates, plus a tray shell)

- `crates/core` - collectors, event pipeline, SQLite storage
  (numbered migrations), queries, monitor registry
  (`crates/core/src/registry.rs` is the single source of truth for
  what is enabled by default).
- `crates/cli` - the `kynoptic` / `kynoptic-ctl` binary with 21
  subcommands: `analyze`, `apps`, `autostart`, `collect`, `dashboard`,
  `db`, `export`, `ghost`, `mcp`, `migrate`, `now`, `presence`, `probe`,
  `query`, `recompute-actors`, `report`, `skill`, `stats`, `topics`,
  `update`, `watchdog`. Includes a local-only web dashboard (read-only
  for activity data; settings are writable via `POST /api/settings`).
  Full command reference: APP.md (kept in sync with the released CLI;
  run `kynoptic --help` for the exact option set of the local binary).
- `crates/dash` - dashboard service and pages (shared by CLI and tray).
- `crates/mcp` - MCP server over stdio JSON-RPC 2.0.
- `crates/tray` - pure Win32 tray shell hosting the collector and
  dashboard in one process.

## MCP tools (six)

`get_current_status`, `get_summary`, `get_timeline`, `get_top_apps`,
`get_anomalies`, `wait_for` - all read locally collected data; nothing
is uploaded.

## Key documents

- [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md) - reproducible performance numbers
  (idle CPU, memory, startup, storage per event, query p95 on a
  1M-event database); the fact-check source for any overhead claims.
- [APP.md](APP.md) - extended workspace docs, including the 40-monitor
  table with sensitivity labels. Of the full 40-monitor list, the 14
  monitors enabled by default are given as an inline list, while the 26
  opt-in monitors are tabulated with sensitivity labels.
- [CODE_NOTES.md](CODE_NOTES.md) - design and carve-out decisions.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) / [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) /
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Build and test

Requirements: Windows 10/11, stable Rust toolchain (MSVC target).

```bash
cargo build --workspace
cargo test --workspace
```
